{{Short description|Result in category theory}}
In mathematics, especially [[category theory]], the '''2-Yoneda lemma''' is a generalization of the [[Yoneda lemma]] to [[2-category|2-categories]]. Precisely, given a contravariant [[pseudofunctor]] <math>F</math> on a category ''C'', it says:<ref>{{harvnb|Kelly|1982|loc=§ 2.4.}}</ref> for each object <math>x</math> in ''C'', the natural functor (evaluation at the identity)
:<math>\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(h_x, F) \to F(x)</math>
is an [[equivalence of categories]], where <math> \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(-, -)</math> denotes (roughly) the category of natural transformations between pseudofunctors on ''C'' and <math>h_x = \operatorname{Hom}(-, x)</math>.

Under the [[Grothendieck construction]], <math>h_x</math> corresponds to the [[comma category]] <math>C \downarrow x</math>. So, the lemma is also frequently stated as:<ref>{{harvnb|Vistoli|2008|loc=§ 3.6.2.}}</ref>
:<math>F(x) \simeq \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C \downarrow x, F),</math>
where <math>F</math> is identified with the [[fibered category]] associated to <math>F</math>.

As an application of this lemma, the [[2-category#Coherence theorem|coherence theorem for bicategories]] holds.

== Sketch of proof ==
First we define the functor in the opposite direction
:<math>\mu : F(x) \to \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(h_x, F)</math>
as follows. Given an object <math>\overline{x}</math> in <math>F(x)</math>, define the natural transformation
:<math>\mu(\overline{x}) : h_x \to F,</math>
that is, <math>\mu(\overline{x})_y : \operatorname{Hom}(y, x) \to F(y),</math> by
:<math>\mu(\overline{x})_y(f) = (Ff) \overline{x}.</math>
(In the below, we shall often drop a subscript for a [[natural transformation]].) Next, given a morphism <math>\varphi : \overline{x} \to x'</math> in <math>F(x)</math>, for <math>f : y \to x</math>, we let <math>\mu(\varphi)(f)</math> be
:<math>(Ff)\varphi : (Ff)\overline{x} \to (Ff)x'.</math>
Then <math>\mu(\varphi) :\mu(\overline{x}) \to \mu(x')</math> is a morphism (a 2-morphism to be precise or a [[Modification (mathematics)|modification]] in the terminology of Bénabou). The rest of the proof is then to show
# The above <math>\mu</math> is a functor,
# <math>e \circ \mu \simeq \operatorname{id}</math>, where <math>e</math> is the evaluation at the identity; i.e., <math>e(\lambda) = \lambda(\operatorname{id}_x),</math> <math>e(\alpha : \lambda \to \rho) = \alpha(\operatorname{id}_x) : \lambda(\operatorname{id}_x) \to \rho(\operatorname{id}_x),</math>
# <math>\mu \circ e \simeq \operatorname{id}.</math>
Claim 1 is clear. As for Claim 2, 
:<math>e(\mu(\overline{x})) = \mu(\overline{x})(\operatorname{id}_x) = F(\operatorname{id}_x) \overline{x} \simeq \operatorname{id}_{F(x)} \overline{x} = \overline{x}</math>
where the isomorphism here comes from the fact that <math>F</math> is a pseudofunctor. Similarly,<math>e(\mu(\varphi)) \simeq \varphi.</math>
For Claim 3, we have:
:<math>\mu(e(\lambda))(f) = (Ff \circ \lambda)(\operatorname{id}_x) \simeq (\lambda \circ h_x f)(\operatorname{id}_x) = \lambda(f).</math>
Similarly for a morphism <math>\alpha : \lambda \to \rho.</math> <math>\square</math>

== ∞-Yoneda ==
Given an [[∞-category]] ''C'', let <math>\widehat{C} = \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C^{op}, \textbf{Kan})</math> be the ∞-category of presheaves on it with values in '''Kan''' = the [[∞-category of Kan complexes]]. Then the ∞-version of the Yoneda embedding <math>C \hookrightarrow \widehat{C}</math> involves some (harmless) choice in the following way.

First, we have the [[hom-functor for ∞-categories|hom-functor]]
:<math>\operatorname{Hom} : C^{op} \times C  \to \textbf{Kan}</math>
that is characterized by a certain [[universal property]] (e.g., [[universal left fibration]]) and is unique up to a unique isomorphism in the homotopy category <math>\operatorname{ho}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C \times C^{op}, \textbf{Kan}).</math><ref>{{harvnb|Cisinski|2023|loc=§ 5.8.1.}}</ref><ref>{{harvnb|8.3.3 Hom-Functors for ∞-Categories in Kerodon}}</ref> Fix one such functor. Then we get the Yoneda embedding functor in the usual way:
:<math>y : C \to \widehat{C}, \, a \mapsto \operatorname{Hom}(-, a),</math>
which turns out to be fully faithful (i.e., an equivalence on the Hom level).<ref>{{harvnb|Cisinski|2023|loc=Theorem 5.8.13. (i).}}</ref> Moreover and more strongly, for each object <math>F</math> in <math>\widehat{C}</math> and object <math>a</math> in <math>C</math>, the evaluation <math>e</math> at the identity (see below)
:<math>\operatorname{Hom}(y(a), F) \to F(a)</math>
is invertible in the ∞-category of large Kan complexes (i.e., Kan complexes living in a universe larger than the given one).<ref>{{harvnb|Cisinski|2023|loc=Theorem 5.8.13. (ii).}}</ref> Here, the evaluation map <math>e</math> refers to the composition
:<math>\operatorname{Hom}(y(a), F) \overset{-(a)}\to \operatorname{Hom}(y(a)(a), F(a)) = \operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Hom}(a, a), F(a)) \to F(a)</math>
where the last map is the restriction to the identity <math>\operatorname{id}_a</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Cisinski|2023|loc=§ 5.8.8.}}</ref>

The ∞-Yoneda lemma is closely related to the matter of [[straightening (category theory)|straightening]] and unstraightening.
